top_5.excerpt: When the engine is hot, the thermostat should be open and coolant should flow through the radiator. P00B7 is set when the engine coolant temperature is very high (above about 117 to 119 °C in documented cases) while the radiator side stays much colde...
top_5.document:
Title: DTC P00B7 - Engine Coolant Flow Low/Performance
Diagnostic Codes: P00B7
Vehicle System: Engine And Transmission
Problem Description: When the engine is hot, the thermostat should be open and coolant should flow through the radiator. P00B7 is set when the engine coolant temperature is very high (above about 117 to 119 °C in documented cases) while the radiator side stays much colder, so too little coolant flows through the radiator. The usual cause is a thermostat stuck closed; low coolant, air in the system, a pump that delivers too little or a blocked radiator have the same effect. If the temperature keeps rising, stop driving to avoid engine damage.
Symptoms: Check engine light on; Coolant warning light; High engine temperature up to overheating; Weak or fluctuating cabin heating
Possible Causes: Thermostat stuck closed (likelihood: high); Low coolant level or air in the cooling system (likelihood: high); Coolant pump delivering too little (impeller, drive; known cases on some engines) (likelihood: medium); Radiator or hoses blocked (likelihood: medium); One of the temperature sensors reading wrong (likelihood: low)
Diagnostic Steps: Connect OBD-II diagnostic scanner and verify active code P00B7 (Engine Coolant Flow Low/Performance). Perform visual and physical inspection of affected components: thermostat, coolant pump, radiator, engine coolant, radiator coolant temperature sensor. Check electrical wiring harnesses and connectors for looseness, corrosion, or pin displacement. Measure reference voltage, ground continuity, and component resistance against manufacturer specifications. Repair guidance: DIY feasible. Estimated labor time: 1-4 hours
Recommended Actions: Prioritize inspection of primary cause: Thermostat stuck closed (likelihood: high). If issue persists, inspect secondary potential fault: Low coolant level or air in the cooling system (likelihood: high). Clear diagnostic trouble codes with scanner after component repair and perform a verification test drive.

top_5.document:
Title: DTC P2B61 - Engine Coolant Flow Control Valve Stuck Closed
Diagnostic Codes: P2B61
Vehicle System: Engine And Transmission
Problem Description: P2B61 indicates that the coolant flow control valve stays closed although the engine computer asks it to open, so coolant cannot reach the radiator path as intended. Jaguar Land Rover uses it on the 2.0-litre Ingenium petrol four (2019–2020): in bulletin JLRTB02030NAS1, P2B61-73 appears with P26CB-72 when the movable shroud that diverts coolant in the electrically controlled pump stays put, and the PCM runs the fans at full speed to prevent overheating; a new pump and PCM software are the fix. FCA lists P2B61-00 for the Alfa Romeo Giulia and Stelvio 2.0 turbo (21-045-19, 21-035-20). Mazda uses the code on SKYACTIV-G engines but labels it a range/performance fault of its coolant control valve circuit.
Symptoms: Radiator fans running constantly at high speed, loud noise from the engine bay; Rising engine temperature under load; Check engine light on
Possible Causes: Valve or diversion shroud mechanically stuck closed (JLR variable coolant pump) (likelihood: high); Engine control software that needs an update (likelihood: medium); Valve drive or its wiring no longer moves the valve (likelihood: low)
Diagnostic Steps: Connect OBD-II diagnostic scanner and verify active code P2B61 (Engine Coolant Flow Control Valve Stuck Closed). Perform visual and physical inspection of affected components: engine coolant flow control valve, wiring harness, ecm. Check electrical wiring harnesses and connectors for looseness, corrosion, or pin displacement. Measure reference voltage, ground continuity, and component resistance against manufacturer specifications. Repair guidance: Professional technician service recommended. Estimated labor time: 0.5-3 hours
Recommended Actions: Prioritize inspection of primary cause: Valve or diversion shroud mechanically stuck closed (JLR variable coolant pump) (likelihood: high). If issue persists, inspect secondary potential fault: Engine control software that needs an update (likelihood: medium). Due to system criticality, have vehicle inspected by an ASE-certified technician.

top_5.document:
Title: DTC U0698 - Lost Communication With Coolant Pump E
Diagnostic Codes: U0698
Vehicle System: Network And Communication
Problem Description: Coolant pump E continues the generic letter series of auxiliary electric pumps after A to D. Mercedes-Benz uses it for the second coolant pump in its low-temperature circuit: bulletin LI20.00-P-076708 lists U0698E4 and U0698E5 in the powertrain control unit N127 together with other LIN devices such as fan, charge-air cooler pump and high-temperature control valve. Affected are the GLC (254) and the 2024 facelift GLE (167); drivers see the check engine lamp, a coolant warning and the radiator fan at maximum speed. On the GLC with control unit software 22A the fix is a software update; otherwise connectors, wiring and intermediate connections on the LIN bus are checked. Pumps like Bosch's PDE take speed commands via PWM or LIN and diagnose themselves.
Symptoms: Check engine light; Coolant warning message; Radiator fan running at full speed
Possible Causes: Powertrain control unit software (Mercedes N127 version 22A) (likelihood: high); LIN wiring or intermediate connector chafed or corroded (likelihood: medium); Pump E electronics failed (likelihood: low)
Diagnostic Steps: Connect OBD-II diagnostic scanner and verify active code U0698 (Lost Communication With Coolant Pump E). Perform visual and physical inspection of affected components: coolant pump e, vehicle bus wiring. Check electrical wiring harnesses and connectors for looseness, corrosion, or pin displacement. Measure reference voltage, ground continuity, and component resistance against manufacturer specifications. Repair guidance: Professional technician service recommended. Estimated labor time: 0.3-3 hours
Recommended Actions: Prioritize inspection of primary cause: Powertrain control unit software (Mercedes N127 version 22A) (likelihood: high). If issue persists, inspect secondary potential fault: LIN wiring or intermediate connector chafed or corroded (likelihood: medium). Due to system criticality, have vehicle inspected by an ASE-certified technician.

top_5.excerpt: P2D8A is the second-fan twin of P2D87: the electronics that power fan 2 signal that they have reached their temperature limit. On cars with two radiator fans the second one usually sits on the other side of the shroud; Porsche, for instance, calls it...
top_5.document:
Title: DTC P2D8A - Fan 2 Control Module Over Temperature
Diagnostic Codes: P2D8A
Vehicle System: Engine And Transmission
Problem Description: P2D8A is the second-fan twin of P2D87: the electronics that power fan 2 signal that they have reached their temperature limit. On cars with two radiator fans the second one usually sits on the other side of the shroud; Porsche, for instance, calls its right-hand fan number 2. No manufacturer publicly documents P2D8A. Since supplier modules such as those from Brose are specified for stable output only up to about 120 °C, heat soak in the engine bay after a hard run, a jammed motor pulling high current or clogged fins that starve the fan of air are the first suspects. CARB requires output devices to be checked for proper response, and a module that throttles itself no longer delivers the requested airflow. Expect higher coolant temperature in traffic and weaker air conditioning.
Symptoms: Second fan slows down or cuts out after long idling; Coolant temperature climbs at standstill; Air conditioning blows warmer
Possible Causes: Stiff or partly blocked fan 2 motor overloading its electronics (likelihood: high); Heat build-up around the module, e.g. clogged fins or damaged air guides (likelihood: medium); Defective temperature sensing or power stage in the fan 2 module (likelihood: medium)
Diagnostic Steps: Connect OBD-II diagnostic scanner and verify active code P2D8A (Fan 2 Control Module Over Temperature). Perform visual and physical inspection of affected components: fan control module 2, wiring harness, ecm. Check electrical wiring harnesses and connectors for looseness, corrosion, or pin displacement. Measure reference voltage, ground continuity, and component resistance against manufacturer specifications. Repair guidance: DIY feasible. Estimated labor time: 1-3 hours
Recommended Actions: Prioritize inspection of primary cause: Stiff or partly blocked fan 2 motor overloading its electronics (likelihood: high). If issue persists, inspect secondary potential fault: Heat build-up around the module, e.g. clogged fins or damaged air guides (likelihood: medium). Clear diagnostic trouble codes with scanner after component repair and perform a verification test drive.

top_5.excerpt: P26CB means the engine coolant pump does not deliver the expected work, typically because the impeller is blocked or turns too slowly. Ford's OBD summaries for hybrids let the pump's own electronics judge this from current and speed: too much current...
top_5.document:
Title: DTC P26CB - Engine Coolant Pump Performance/Stuck Off
Diagnostic Codes: P26CB
Vehicle System: Engine And Transmission
Problem Description: P26CB means the engine coolant pump does not deliver the expected work, typically because the impeller is blocked or turns too slowly. Ford's OBD summaries for hybrids let the pump's own electronics judge this from current and speed: too much current at too low a speed through four restart attempts is reported over LIN, and the PCM records P26CB after five seconds. Genesis campaign 916G (GV70 3.5 T, 2024–2025) replaces the electric pump of the water-cooled charge air cooler because a stuck impeller set P26CB. Jaguar Land Rover bulletin JLRTB02030NAS1 links it on Ingenium 2.0 L petrol engines to a switchable mechanical pump whose diverter shroud no longer moves, making the fans run at full speed. Toyota's A25A engines log it as speed stuck. Overheating protection may cut power.
Symptoms: Check engine lamp on; Cooling fans running constantly at high speed; Rising engine temperature or reduced power
Possible Causes: Seized or obstructed impeller in the electric pump (likelihood: high); Diverter shroud of a switchable mechanical pump not moving (likelihood: medium); Worn pump motor or bearing drawing excessive current (likelihood: medium); Engine module logic needing a software update (likelihood: low)
Diagnostic Steps: Connect OBD-II diagnostic scanner and verify active code P26CB (Engine Coolant Pump Performance/Stuck Off). Perform visual and physical inspection of affected components: engine coolant pump, pump motor. Check electrical wiring harnesses and connectors for looseness, corrosion, or pin displacement. Measure reference voltage, ground continuity, and component resistance against manufacturer specifications. Repair guidance: Professional technician service recommended. Estimated labor time: 0.3-4 hours
Recommended Actions: Prioritize inspection of primary cause: Seized or obstructed impeller in the electric pump (likelihood: high). If issue persists, inspect secondary potential fault: Diverter shroud of a switchable mechanical pump not moving (likelihood: medium). Due to system criticality, have vehicle inspected by an ASE-certified technician.

top_10.title: DTC P0117 - Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor 1 Circuit Low
top_10.excerpt: The engine coolant temperature sensor 1 is an NTC thermistor: the control module feeds 5 V through a resistor, and as the coolant warms the resistance and signal voltage fall. Its value drives cold-start enrichment, idle speed, ignition timing, the r...
top_10.document:
Title: DTC P0117 - Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor 1 Circuit Low
Diagnostic Codes: P0117
Vehicle System: Engine And Transmission
Problem Description: The engine coolant temperature sensor 1 is an NTC thermistor: the control module feeds 5 V through a resistor, and as the coolant warms the resistance and signal voltage fall. Its value drives cold-start enrichment, idle speed, ignition timing, the radiator fan and the release of closed-loop mixture control. Some Ford engines measure cylinder head temperature instead and calculate a coolant value from it. P0117 means the signal voltage is too low, so the sensor would report an implausibly hot engine (around 140–160 °C). Usual causes are a signal wire shorted to ground, coolant or moisture in the connector, or an internally shorted sensor. Limits: GM below 55 ohms, Ford petrol below 0.244 V for 5 s, Ford diesel below 0.10 V, Mitsubishi below 0.1 V for 2 s. Possible Causes: Signal wire shorted to ground (chafing, pinched harness) (likelihood: high); Sensor shorted internally or coolant inside the sensor (likelihood: high); Moisture or coolant in the connector (likelihood: medium); Engine control module faulty (likelihood: low)
Diagnostic Steps: Connect OBD-II diagnostic scanner and verify active code P0117 (Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor 1 Circuit Low). Perform visual and physical inspection of affected components: engine coolant temperature sensor, engine coolant temperature sensor wiring. Check electrical wiring harnesses and connectors for looseness, corrosion, or pin displacement. Measure reference voltage, ground continuity, and component resistance against manufacturer specifications. Repair guidance: DIY feasible. Estimated labor time: 0.3-1.5 hours
Recommended Actions: Prioritize inspection of primary cause: Signal wire shorted to ground (chafing, pinched harness) (likelihood: high). If issue persists, inspect secondary potential fault: Sensor shorted internally or coolant inside the sensor (likelihood: high). Clear diagnostic trouble codes with scanner after component repair and perform a verification test drive.

Title: DTC P26B1 - Engine Coolant Bypass Valve A Stuck Closed
Diagnostic Codes: P26B1
Vehicle System: Engine And Transmission
Problem Description: P26B1 reports that valve A does not open when it should. The best documented user is the Volkswagen group plug-in hybrids. Porsche stores P26B100 in the thermal management unit (TME) of the 2019–2022 Cayenne E-Hybrid and the 2019–2021 Panamera E-Hybrid for the valve that admits engine coolant to the heating circuit once the engine passes 40 °C. The TME infers its state from the gap between two coolant temperatures, with 7 °C as the limit, and certain conditions caused false entries; bulletins 116/22 and 193/22 reprogram the TME. Bentley found the same code on 2022 Flying Spur Hybrids (N91 valve) and also fixes it by software. A real fault leaves the heating circuit without engine heat and can affect warm-up strategy.
Symptoms: Check engine light, sometimes only intermittent; Cabin heat relies on the electric heater longer than usual; Possible rise in engine temperature under load
Possible Causes: Thermal management software misjudging the valve (Porsche, Bentley) (likelihood: high); Valve seized closed by deposits or a failed actuator (likelihood: medium); Swapped or kinked coolant lines after repair (likelihood: low); Drifting coolant temperature sensor used for the check (likelihood: low)
Diagnostic Steps: Connect OBD-II diagnostic scanner and verify active code P26B1 (Engine Coolant Bypass Valve A Stuck Closed). Perform visual and physical inspection of affected components: coolant bypass valve a, thermostat housing. Check electrical wiring harnesses and connectors for looseness, corrosion, or pin displacement. Measure reference voltage, ground continuity, and component resistance against manufacturer specifications. Repair guidance: Professional technician service recommended. Estimated labor time: 0.5-3 hours
Recommended Actions: Prioritize inspection of primary cause: Thermal management software misjudging the valve (Porsche, Bentley) (likelihood: high). If issue persists, inspect secondary potential fault: Valve seized closed by deposits or a failed actuator (likelihood: medium). Due to system criticality, have vehicle inspected by an ASE-certified technician.

Title: DTC P00B6 - Radiator Coolant Temperature/Engine Coolant Temperature Correlation
Diagnostic Codes: P00B6
Vehicle System: Engine And Transmission
Problem Description: The radiator coolant temperature sensor is an NTC thermistor that measures coolant temperature on the radiator side, typically at the radiator outlet; the exact position depends on the manufacturer. Together with the engine coolant temperature sensor it gives a second measuring point, which the control module uses to diagnose the thermostat and coolant flow, for example on engines with an electrically heated map-controlled thermostat. After a long standstill (eight hours in a documented case) engine and radiator should be at the same temperature. P00B6 is set at the next start when the engine and radiator coolant temperature sensors differ by more than a threshold that may depend on intake air temperature. A detected engine block heater cancels the test. From this alone the control module cannot tell which sensor is wrong.
Symptoms: Check engine light on; Usually no noticeable symptoms
Possible Causes: Radiator coolant temperature sensor drifting (likelihood: high); Engine coolant temperature sensor drifting (likelihood: high); Contact resistance at a connector (likelihood: medium); Retrofitted engine preheater or auxiliary heater not detected by the system (likelihood: medium)
Diagnostic Steps: Connect OBD-II diagnostic scanner and verify active code P00B6 (Radiator Coolant Temperature/Engine Coolant Temperature Correlation). Perform visual and physical inspection of affected components: radiator coolant temperature sensor, engine coolant temperature sensor, sensor wiring. Check electrical wiring harnesses and connectors for looseness, corrosion, or pin displacement. Measure reference voltage, ground continuity, and component resistance against manufacturer specifications. Repair guidance: DIY feasible. Estimated labor time: 0.5-1.5 hours
Recommended Actions: Prioritize inspection of primary cause: Radiator coolant temperature sensor drifting (likelihood: high). If issue persists, inspect secondary potential fault: Engine coolant temperature sensor drifting (likelihood: high). Clear diagnostic trouble codes with scanner after component repair and perform a verification test drive.

Title: DTC U0617 - Lost Communication With Engine Coolant Bypass Valve C
Diagnostic Codes: U0617
Vehicle System: Network And Communication
Problem Description: Unlike its LIN-based neighbours, GM uses U0617 for a coolant bypass valve whose position sensor transmits SENT frames (SAE J2716) to the engine controller. The tables 25OBDG03B and 25OBDG04B count a failure when the input hardware flags a message fault, when pulses arrive but the newest frame is older than 6.25 ms, or when the SENT pin voltage stays above or below a controller limit while frames go stale. Four failures within a five-second window set the code as Type B over two trips; the 2019 table 19OBDG03D still ran it as Type A after one trip. Suppliers such as Rheinmetall offer coolant valves with SENT position feedback. Typical causes are wiring and connector faults on the three-wire sensor line. The valve may stop being regulated, so warm-up and heater output can suffer.
Symptoms: Check engine light (on GM after two trips, on 2019 calibrations after one); Slow warm-up or reduced heater output; Possibly further coolant valve codes stored at the same time
Possible Causes: SENT signal, 5 V supply or ground wire of the valve position sensor open or shorted (likelihood: high); Corroded or loose connector at the valve (likelihood: medium); Position sensor inside the valve failed (usually replaced with the valve) (likelihood: medium); SENT input of the engine controller faulty (likelihood: low)
Diagnostic Steps: Connect OBD-II diagnostic scanner and verify active code U0617 (Lost Communication With Engine Coolant Bypass Valve C). Perform visual and physical inspection of affected components: coolant bypass valve c, sensor wiring. Check electrical wiring harnesses and connectors for looseness, corrosion, or pin displacement. Measure reference voltage, ground continuity, and component resistance against manufacturer specifications. Repair guidance: DIY feasible. Estimated labor time: 0.5-2.5 hours
Recommended Actions: Prioritize inspection of primary cause: SENT signal, 5 V supply or ground wire of the valve position sensor open or shorted (likelihood: high). If issue persists, inspect secondary potential fault: Corroded or loose connector at the valve (likelihood: medium). Clear diagnostic trouble codes with scanner after component repair and perform a verification test drive.

top_10.document:
Title: DTC P2B58 - Engine Coolant Flow Control Valve Motor Current High
Diagnostic Codes: P2B58
Vehicle System: Engine And Transmission
Problem Description: P2B58 reports that the electric motor driving the engine coolant flow control valve draws too much current. GM documents the check for its 3.0-litre inline-six Duramax diesel: in the 2025 table 25OBDG04B the driver stage flags a current above 5.5 A, and 80 failures in 100 samples taken every 12.5 ms set a Type B fault, so the MIL follows on the second trip. Enabling needs more than 11 V on the powertrain relay and an engine that is not cranking. A seized rotary valve, debris in the housing or a motor with shorted windings are typical reasons. GM bulletin 21-NA-149 lists P2B58 for LM2 trucks with a chafed engine harness. Heating and warm-up may suffer while the valve is stuck.
Symptoms: MIL on after the second drive with the fault; Slow warm-up or weak cabin heat; Fans may run more often as a precaution
Possible Causes: Rotary valve stiff or seized from deposits or debris in the housing (likelihood: high); Valve motor with shorted turns (likelihood: medium); Chafed engine harness on GM LM2 (bulletin 21-NA-149) (likelihood: medium)
Diagnostic Steps: Connect OBD-II diagnostic scanner and verify active code P2B58 (Engine Coolant Flow Control Valve Motor Current High). Perform visual and physical inspection of affected components: engine coolant flow control valve, wiring harness, ecm. Check electrical wiring harnesses and connectors for looseness, corrosion, or pin displacement. Measure reference voltage, ground continuity, and component resistance against manufacturer specifications. Repair guidance: Professional technician service recommended. Estimated labor time: 1-10 hours
Recommended Actions: Prioritize inspection of primary cause: Rotary valve stiff or seized from deposits or debris in the housing (likelihood: high). If issue persists, inspect secondary potential fault: Valve motor with shorted turns (likelihood: medium). Due to system criticality, have vehicle inspected by an ASE-certified technician.

Title: DTC P0316 - Engine Misfire Detected on Startup (First 1000 Revolutions)
Diagnostic Codes: P0316
Vehicle System: Engine And Transmission
Problem Description: P0316 concerns misfire within the first 1,000 revolutions after start. CARB requires a pending code here after the first exceedance of the emissions-relevant rate (later in the drive only after the fourth) and the warning light if it recurs at the next start. Ford sets P0316 in addition to the cylinder code; GM evaluates the start within P0300–P0308 without its own code. Typical causes are water in the plug wells (Mazda Tribute bulletin: blocked drain in the valve cover channel), coils that arc when cold and damp, injectors that drip after switch-off and over-rich starting – Ford traced cases on the 2.7 EcoBoost to engine software or leaking direct injectors.
Symptoms: Check engine light (usually with P0300/P030x); Rough running right after a cold start, then normal; Delayed start, fuel smell at start
Possible Causes: Moisture or water in the plug wells, coils arcing when cold or damp (likelihood: high); Leaking injectors (fuel drips after switch-off, over-rich start) (likelihood: medium); Worn or sooted spark plugs that only fire cleanly when warm (likelihood: medium); Wrong temperature sensor value or engine software (likelihood: low)
Diagnostic Steps: Connect OBD-II diagnostic scanner and verify active code P0316 (Engine Misfire Detected on Startup (First 1000 Revolutions)). Perform visual and physical inspection of affected components: ignition coils, spark plugs, fuel injectors. Check electrical wiring harnesses and connectors for looseness, corrosion, or pin displacement. Measure reference voltage, ground continuity, and component resistance against manufacturer specifications. Repair guidance: DIY feasible. Estimated labor time: 0.3-4 hours
Recommended Actions: Prioritize inspection of primary cause: Moisture or water in the plug wells, coils arcing when cold or damp (likelihood: high). If issue persists, inspect secondary potential fault: Leaking injectors (fuel drips after switch-off, over-rich start) (likelihood: medium). Clear diagnostic trouble codes with scanner after component repair and perform a verification test drive.

Title: DTC P2314 - Ignition Coil E Secondary Circuit
Diagnostic Codes: P2314
Vehicle System: Engine And Transmission
Problem Description: P2314 reports a fault on the high-voltage side of coil E, which only five-cylinder and larger engines have; it normally fires cylinder 5. The control line may be perfectly sound; what failed is the energy reaching the plug or the combustion that should follow. FCA is the documented user: on the 3.6-litre Pentastar V6 of 2015–2016 Caravan and Town & Country models it is coil 5 secondary circuit with insufficient ionization, one of six such codes that bulletin 18-069-16 tied to a faulty PCM in a short build window. GM, Ford and VW tables cover coil E only on the primary side (P2312, P2313, P0355). Practical checks are the plug of cylinder 5, the boot and a swap test with a neighbouring coil; if the code stays with the cylinder, look at the plug or the module.
Symptoms: Check engine light on; Misfire on cylinder 5; Rough idle, slight vibration
Possible Causes: Spark plug of cylinder 5 worn or fouled (likelihood: high); Coil E secondary winding or boot damaged (likelihood: medium); PCM fault on FCA vans from the 2015 build window (likelihood: low)
Diagnostic Steps: Connect OBD-II diagnostic scanner and verify active code P2314 (Ignition Coil E Secondary Circuit). Perform visual and physical inspection of affected components: ignition coil, spark plug. Check electrical wiring harnesses and connectors for looseness, corrosion, or pin displacement. Measure reference voltage, ground continuity, and component resistance against manufacturer specifications. Repair guidance: DIY feasible. Estimated labor time: 0.3-3 hours
Recommended Actions: Prioritize inspection of primary cause: Spark plug of cylinder 5 worn or fouled (likelihood: high). If issue persists, inspect secondary potential fault: Coil E secondary winding or boot damaged (likelihood: medium). Clear diagnostic trouble codes with scanner after component repair and perform a verification test drive.

Title: DTC P2E5C - Cylinder 4 Alternative Fuel Misfire Detected
Diagnostic Codes: P2E5C
Vehicle System: Engine And Transmission
Problem Description: P2E5C is stored when the misfire counter blames cylinder 4 while gas is being burned; in petrol mode the code would be P0304. No manufacturer documents P2E5C publicly, and Deutz's fault list for its eControls LPG, CNG and bi-fuel engines reports such events with the ordinary P0301 to P0304. On four-cylinder engines cylinder 4 is the last one in the block. Ignition is the main gas-related suspect: NGK points out that a gas/air charge needs a clearly higher firing voltage than petrol, which loads the coils and wears the plugs faster, and the US Department of Energy notes that natural gas reacts more sensitively to spark quality. A coil or plug that still works on petrol can therefore drop out on gas alone. Check plug type and gap for gas, coil and boot, then move the coil to another cylinder.
Symptoms: Misfire mainly under load or acceleration on gas; Engine runs cleanly after switching to petrol; Check engine light, flashing during heavy misfire
Possible Causes: Spark plug on cylinder 4 worn or unsuited for gas (gap too wide, wrong heat range) (likelihood: high); Coil or plug boot on cylinder 4 breaking down under the higher firing voltage (likelihood: high); Gas injector on cylinder 4 sticking or delivering too little (likelihood: medium)
Diagnostic Steps: Connect OBD-II diagnostic scanner and verify active code P2E5C (Cylinder 4 Alternative Fuel Misfire Detected). Perform visual and physical inspection of affected components: alt fuel injector cyl 4, ignition coil cyl 4. Check electrical wiring harnesses and connectors for looseness, corrosion, or pin displacement. Measure reference voltage, ground continuity, and component resistance against manufacturer specifications. Repair guidance: DIY feasible. Estimated labor time: 0.3-3 hours
Recommended Actions: Prioritize inspection of primary cause: Spark plug on cylinder 4 worn or unsuited for gas (gap too wide, wrong heat range) (likelihood: high). If issue persists, inspect secondary potential fault: Coil or plug boot on cylinder 4 breaking down under the higher firing voltage (likelihood: high). Clear diagnostic trouble codes with scanner after component repair and perform a verification test drive.

Title: DTC P2E5E - Cylinder 6 Alternative Fuel Misfire Detected
Diagnostic Codes: P2E5E
Vehicle System: Engine And Transmission
Problem Description: P2E5E names cylinder 6 as the misfiring one while the engine runs on alternative fuel; P0306 is its petrol twin. No manufacturer documents the code openly. On inline sixes cylinder 6 is the rearmost. With liquid propane injection, fuel turning to vapour in the rail is a known gas-specific cause: Roush CleanTech's diagnostic manual names running in the vapour region as a reason for P03xx misfire, a Ford patent notes that propane left in a hot rail boils off after shutdown and expands about 250-fold, and an Agility patent describes vapour forming when pressure sags along a rail feeding its injectors in series, so too little fuel is metered. Note whether misfire follows hot restarts or a low tank. A Texas training manual on propane conversions recommends the scan tool's cylinder balance test to confirm the cylinder.
Symptoms: Misfire or rough running shortly after a hot restart; Long cranking time when the engine is warm; Check engine light
Possible Causes: Gas or liquid-propane injector on cylinder 6 sticking or leaking (likelihood: high); Propane vapour in the liquid-injection rail (hot restart, low rail or tank pressure) (likelihood: medium); Plug or coil on cylinder 6 failing under gas (likelihood: medium); Low tank pressure in cold weather or nearly empty tank (likelihood: low)
Diagnostic Steps: Connect OBD-II diagnostic scanner and verify active code P2E5E (Cylinder 6 Alternative Fuel Misfire Detected). Perform visual and physical inspection of affected components: alt fuel injector cyl 6, ignition coil cyl 6. Check electrical wiring harnesses and connectors for looseness, corrosion, or pin displacement. Measure reference voltage, ground continuity, and component resistance against manufacturer specifications. Repair guidance: Professional technician service recommended. Estimated labor time: 0.5-5 hours
Recommended Actions: Prioritize inspection of primary cause: Gas or liquid-propane injector on cylinder 6 sticking or leaking (likelihood: high). If issue persists, inspect secondary potential fault: Propane vapour in the liquid-injection rail (hot restart, low rail or tank pressure) (likelihood: medium). Due to system criticality, have vehicle inspected by an ASE-certified technician.

Title: DTC P2A2F - Alternative Fuel Tank Shutoff Valve E Control Circuit Performance/Stuck Off
Diagnostic Codes: P2A2F
Vehicle System: Engine And Transmission
Problem Description: P2A2F signals that valve E was energized but the system did not see the expected gas flow from that cylinder. No manufacturer publishes this code or its test conditions; CARB only requires output components to be checked for a proper reaction to commands. New Flyer's bulletin explains that its tank solenoids switch on while the starter spins the engine to about 400 rpm. A weak battery or a voltage dip during cranking can therefore leave a coil unable to lift its armature, which looks exactly like a valve that hangs shut. GM's bi-fuel Impala regulates gas to 468 to 896 kPa, a useful reference when checking the low-pressure side. Contamination and a closed manual valve remain obvious mechanical causes.
Symptoms: Check engine light; Cylinder E does not empty; Fault appears mainly after cold or weak-battery starts
Possible Causes: Voltage drop during cranking, coil cannot lift the armature (likelihood: medium); Contaminated or sticking valve E (likelihood: medium); Manual valve on cylinder E closed (likelihood: low)
Diagnostic Steps: Connect OBD-II diagnostic scanner and verify active code P2A2F (Alternative Fuel Tank Shutoff Valve E Control Circuit Performance/Stuck Off). Perform visual and physical inspection of affected components: alt fuel tank shutoff valve e, wiring harness, afcm. Check electrical wiring harnesses and connectors for looseness, corrosion, or pin displacement. Measure reference voltage, ground continuity, and component resistance against manufacturer specifications. Repair guidance: Professional technician service recommended. Estimated labor time: 0.5-4 hours
Recommended Actions: Prioritize inspection of primary cause: Voltage drop during cranking, coil cannot lift the armature (likelihood: medium). If issue persists, inspect secondary potential fault: Contaminated or sticking valve E (likelihood: medium). Due to system criticality, have vehicle inspected by an ASE-certified technician.

Ford sets P0316 in addition to the cylinder code; GM evaluates the start within P0300–P0308 without its own code. Typical causes are water in the plug wells (Mazda Tribute bulletin: blocked drain in the valve cover channel), coils that arc when cold and damp, injectors that drip after switch-off and over-rich starting – Ford traced cases on the 2.7 EcoBoost to engine software or leaking direct injectors.
Symptoms: Check engine light (usually with P0300/P030x); Rough running right after a cold start, then normal; Delayed start, fuel smell at start
Possible Causes: Moisture or water in the plug wells, coils arcing when cold or damp (likelihood: high); Leaking injectors (fuel drips after switch-off, over-rich start) (likelihood: medium); Worn or sooted spark plugs that only fire cleanly when warm (likelihood: medium); Wrong temperature sensor value or engine software (likelihood: low)
Diagnostic Steps: Connect OBD-II diagnostic scanner and verify active code P0316 (Engine Misfire Detected on Startup (First 1000 Revolutions)). Perform visual and physical inspection of affected components: ignition coils, spark plugs, fuel injectors. Check electrical wiring harnesses and connectors for looseness, corrosion, or pin displacement. Measure reference voltage, ground continuity, and component resistance against manufacturer specifications. Repair guidance: DIY feasible. Estimated labor time: 0.3-4 hours
Recommended Actions: Prioritize inspection of primary cause: Moisture or water in the plug wells, coils arcing when cold or damp (likelihood: high). If issue persists, inspect secondary potential fault: Leaking injectors (fuel drips after switch-off, over-rich start) (likelihood: medium). Clear diagnostic trouble codes with scanner after component repair and perform a verification test drive.

Title: DTC P2314 - Ignition Coil E Secondary Circuit
Diagnostic Codes: P2314
Vehicle System: Engine And Transmission
Problem Description: P2314 reports a fault on the high-voltage side of coil E, which only five-cylinder and larger engines have; it normally fires cylinder 5. The control line may be perfectly sound; what failed is the energy reaching the plug or the combustion that should follow. FCA is the documented user: on the 3.6-litre Pentastar V6 of 2015–2016 Caravan and Town & Country models it is coil 5 secondary circuit with insufficient ionization, one of six such codes that bulletin 18-069-16 tied to a faulty PCM in a short build window. GM, Ford and VW tables cover coil E only on the primary side (P2312, P2313, P0355). Practical checks are the plug of cylinder 5, the boot and a swap test with a neighbouring coil; if the code stays with the cylinder, look at the plug or the module.
Symptoms: Check engine light on; Misfire on cylinder 5; Rough idle, slight vibration
Possible Causes: Spark plug of cylinder 5 worn or fouled (likelihood: high); Coil E secondary winding or boot damaged (likelihood: medium); PCM fault on FCA vans from the 2015 build window (likelihood: low)
Diagnostic Steps: Connect OBD-II diagnostic scanner and verify active code P2314 (Ignition Coil E Secondary Circuit). Perform visual and physical inspection of affected components: ignition coil, spark plug. Check electrical wiring harnesses and connectors for looseness, corrosion, or pin displacement. Measure reference voltage, ground continuity, and component resistance against manufacturer specifications. Repair guidance: DIY feasible. Estimated labor time: 0.3-3 hours
Recommended Actions: Prioritize inspection of primary cause: Spark plug of cylinder 5 worn or fouled (likelihood: high). If issue persists, inspect secondary potential fault: Coil E secondary winding or boot damaged (likelihood: medium). top_10.document:
Title: DTC P2E5C - Cylinder 4 Alternative Fuel Misfire Detected
Diagnostic Codes: P2E5C
Vehicle System: Engine And Transmission
Problem Description: P2E5C is stored when the misfire counter blames cylinder 4 while gas is being burned; in petrol mode the code would be P0304. No manufacturer documents P2E5C publicly, and Deutz's fault list for its eControls LPG, CNG and bi-fuel engines reports such events with the ordinary P0301 to P0304. On four-cylinder engines cylinder 4 is the last one in the block. Ignition is the main gas-related suspect: NGK points out that a gas/air charge needs a clearly higher firing voltage than petrol, which loads the coils and wears the plugs faster, and the US Department of Energy notes that natural gas reacts more sensitively to spark quality. A coil or plug that still works on petrol can therefore drop out on gas alone. Check plug type and gap for gas, coil and boot, then move the coil to another cylinder.
Symptoms: Misfire mainly under load or acceleration on gas; Engine runs cleanly after switching to petrol; Check engine light, flashing during heavy misfire
Possible Causes: Spark plug on cylinder 4 worn or unsuited for gas (gap too wide, wrong heat range) (likelihood: high); Coil or plug boot on cylinder 4 breaking down under the higher firing voltage (likelihood: high); Gas injector on cylinder 4 sticking or delivering too little (likelihood: medium)
Diagnostic Steps: Connect OBD-II diagnostic scanner and verify active code P2E5C (Cylinder 4 Alternative Fuel Misfire Detected). Perform visual and physical inspection of affected components: alt fuel injector cyl 4, ignition coil cyl 4. Check electrical wiring harnesses and connectors for looseness, corrosion, or pin displacement. Measure reference voltage, ground continuity, and component resistance against manufacturer specifications. Repair guidance: DIY feasible. Estimated labor time: 0.3-3 hours
Recommended Actions: Prioritize inspection of primary cause: Spark plug on cylinder 4 worn or unsuited for gas (gap too wide, wrong heat range) (likelihood: high). If issue persists, inspect secondary potential fault: Coil or plug boot on cylinder 4 breaking down under the higher firing voltage (likelihood: high). Clear diagnostic trouble codes with scanner after component repair and perform a verification test drive.

Title: DTC P2E5E - Cylinder 6 Alternative Fuel Misfire Detected
Diagnostic Codes: P2E5E
Vehicle System: Engine And Transmission
Problem Description: P2E5E names cylinder 6 as the misfiring one while the engine runs on alternative fuel; P0306 is its petrol twin. No manufacturer documents the code openly. On inline sixes cylinder 6 is the rearmost. With liquid propane injection, fuel turning to vapour in the rail is a known gas-specific cause: Roush CleanTech's diagnostic manual names running in the vapour region as a reason for P03xx misfire, a Ford patent notes that propane left in a hot rail boils off after shutdown and expands about 250-fold, and an Agility patent describes vapour forming when pressure sags along a rail feeding its injectors in series, so too little fuel is metered. Note whether misfire follows hot restarts or a low tank. A Texas training manual on propane conversions recommends the scan tool's cylinder balance test to confirm the cylinder.
Symptoms: Misfire or rough running shortly after a hot restart; Long cranking time when the engine is warm; Check engine light
Possible Causes: Gas or liquid-propane injector on cylinder 6 sticking or leaking (likelihood: high); Propane vapour in the liquid-injection rail (hot restart, low rail or tank pressure) (likelihood: medium); Plug or coil on cylinder 6 failing under gas (likelihood: medium); Low tank pressure in cold weather or nearly empty tank (likelihood: low)
Diagnostic Steps: Connect OBD-II diagnostic scanner and verify active code P2E5E (Cylinder 6 Alternative Fuel Misfire Detected). Perform visual and physical inspection of affected components: alt fuel injector cyl 6, ignition coil cyl 6. Check electrical wiring harnesses and connectors for looseness, corrosion, or pin displacement. Measure reference voltage, ground continuity, and component resistance against manufacturer specifications. Repair guidance: Professional technician service recommended. Estimated labor time: 0.5-5 hours
Recommended Actions: Prioritize inspection of primary cause: Gas or liquid-propane injector on cylinder 6 sticking or leaking (likelihood: high). If issue persists, inspect secondary potential fault: Propane vapour in the liquid-injection rail (hot restart, low rail or tank pressure) (likelihood: medium). Due to system criticality, have vehicle inspected by an ASE-certified technician.

Title: DTC P2A2F - Alternative Fuel Tank Shutoff Valve E Control Circuit Performance/Stuck Off
Diagnostic Codes: P2A2F
Vehicle System: Engine And Transmission
Problem Description: P2A2F signals that valve E was energized but the system did not see the expected gas flow from that cylinder. No manufacturer publishes this code or its test conditions; CARB only requires output components to be checked for a proper reaction to commands. New Flyer's bulletin explains that its tank solenoids switch on while the starter spins the engine to about 400 rpm. A weak battery or a voltage dip during cranking can therefore leave a coil unable to lift its armature, which looks exactly like a valve that hangs shut. GM's bi-fuel Impala regulates gas to 468 to 896 kPa, a useful reference when checking the low-pressure side. Contamination and a closed manual valve remain obvious mechanical causes.
Symptoms: Check engine light; Cylinder E does not empty; Fault appears mainly after cold or weak-battery starts
Possible Causes: Voltage drop during cranking, coil cannot lift the armature (likelihood: medium); Contaminated or sticking valve E (likelihood: medium); Manual valve on cylinder E closed (likelihood: low)
Diagnostic Steps: Connect OBD-II diagnostic scanner and verify active code P2A2F (Alternative Fuel Tank Shutoff Valve E Control Circuit Performance/Stuck Off). Perform visual and physical inspection of affected components: alt fuel tank shutoff valve e, wiring harness, afcm. Check electrical wiring harnesses and connectors for looseness, corrosion, or pin displacement. Measure reference voltage, ground continuity, and component resistance against manufacturer specifications. Repair guidance: Professional technician service recommended. Estimated labor time: 0.5-4 hours
Recommended Actions: Prioritize inspection of primary cause: Voltage drop during cranking, coil cannot lift the armature (likelihood: medium). If issue persists, inspect secondary potential fault: Contaminated or sticking valve E (likelihood: medium). Due to system criticality, have vehicle inspected by an ASE-certified technician.

Title: DTC P2320 - Ignition Coil G Secondary Circuit
Diagnostic Codes: P2320
Vehicle System: Engine And Transmission
Problem Description: P2320 points at the high-voltage half of coil G, normally the coil on cylinder 7, so only engines with seven or more cylinders can log it. FCA is the maker on record: STAR case S2118000002 from March 2021 for the 2020–2021 Ram 1500 names P2320 as coil 7 secondary circuit with insufficient ionization. Insufficient ionization means the PCM saw too little ion current across the plug gap after the spark, a sign of weak or missing combustion in that cylinder. FCA's first step is a pull-push-pull check of the coil connector to see whether it is fully seated and locked, followed by normal diagnosis if the code returns. A shorted control wire on the same coil instead sets P2318/P2319, an open one P0357. Expect a rough-running engine and often P0307 alongside.
Symptoms: Check engine light on; Misfire felt on cylinder 7, often with P0307; Engine shakes at idle or under load
Possible Causes: Coil 7 connector not fully seated or latched (FCA) (likelihood: high); Spark plug of cylinder 7 worn, fouled or with wrong gap (likelihood: medium); Coil G secondary winding or boot breaking down (likelihood: medium); Ion-current evaluation in the PCM faulty (likelihood: low)
Diagnostic Steps: Connect OBD-II diagnostic scanner and verify active code P2320 (Ignition Coil G Secondary Circuit). Perform visual and physical inspection of affected components: ignition coil, spark plug. Check electrical wiring harnesses and connectors for looseness, corrosion, or pin displacement. Measure reference voltage, ground continuity, and component resistance against manufacturer specifications. Repair guidance: DIY feasible. Estimated labor time: 0.2-2 hours
Recommended Actions: Prioritize inspection of primary cause: Coil 7 connector not fully seated or latched (FCA) (likelihood: high). If issue persists, inspect secondary potential fault: Spark plug of cylinder 7 worn, fouled or with wrong gap (likelihood: medium). Clear diagnostic trouble codes with scanner after component repair and perform a verification test drive.

Title: DTC P2335 - Ignition Coil L Secondary Circuit
Diagnostic Codes: P2335
Vehicle System: Engine And Transmission
Problem Description: P2335 closes the ignition coil block of J2012: a fault on the high-voltage side of coil L, the twelfth coil. No manufacturer documents this code publicly, and none of the reviewed ion-sensing or secondary-monitoring documents reaches past coil 8. Its practical relevance is therefore small; a V12 with a failing coil L, a cracked boot or a worn plug on the last cylinder will normally report it as misfire on cylinder 12 (P0312), and with catalyst-damaging misfire CARB rules require the MIL to flash. If the code does appear, swap coil and plug with another cylinder of the same bank and see whether the fault follows. P2333/P2334 belong to the primary circuit of the same coil; P2332 is the neighbouring coil K secondary code.
Symptoms: Check engine light on, possibly flashing with heavy misfire; Misfire on cylinder 12 (P0312)
Possible Causes: Spark plug of cylinder 12 worn (likelihood: high); Coil L boot cracked (likelihood: medium); Coil L secondary winding weak (likelihood: medium)
Diagnostic Steps: Connect OBD-II diagnostic scanner and verify active code P2335 (Ignition Coil L Secondary Circuit). Perform visual and physical inspection of affected components: ignition coil, spark plug. Check electrical wiring harnesses and connectors for looseness, corrosion, or pin displacement. Measure reference voltage, ground continuity, and component resistance against manufacturer specifications. Repair guidance: Professional technician service recommended. Estimated labor time: 0.5-4 hours
Recommended Actions: Prioritize inspection of primary cause: Spark plug of cylinder 12 worn (likelihood: high). If issue persists, inspect secondary potential fault: Coil L boot cracked (likelihood: medium). Due to system criticality, have vehicle inspected by an ASE-certified technician.

Title: DTC P06D1 - Internal Control Module Ignition Coil Control Performance
Diagnostic Codes: P06D1
Vehicle System: Engine And Transmission
Problem Description: On ignition systems where the coils are driven through a separate driver chip inside the engine module, P06D1 reports that this internal coil control does not work correctly. Ford checks the communication with the coil driver chip continuously and sets the code within 1 s at 200–3200 rpm, positive torque and 11–16 V. GM Europe's V6 (Saab 9-5 2.8 T) reports it as an internal engine module fault with the lamp after two trips. Misfires or rough running can follow if coils are no longer fired correctly. Primary circuit faults of individual coils are P0351–P0360, driver shorts P2300 ff. Check supply and ground, look for software updates; otherwise the module is the likely cause.
Symptoms: Check engine light; Misfires or rough running; Possibly no start
Possible Causes: Coil driver chip or internal communication in the engine module faulty (likelihood: high); Engine module software (likelihood: medium); Supply or ground problem at the module (likelihood: medium); Shorted coil overloading the driver (likelihood: low)
Diagnostic Steps: Connect OBD-II diagnostic scanner and verify active code P06D1 (Internal Control Module Ignition Coil Control Performance). Perform visual and physical inspection of affected components: engine control module, ignition coil driver, ignition coils. Check electrical wiring harnesses and connectors for looseness, corrosion, or pin displacement. Measure reference voltage, ground continuity, and component resistance against manufacturer specifications. Repair guidance: Professional technician service recommended. Title: DTC P2A2E - Alternative Fuel Tank Shutoff Valve E Control Circuit/Open
Diagnostic Codes: P2A2E
Vehicle System: Engine And Transmission
Problem Description: P2A2E is the open-circuit fault for shutoff valve E, the last letter of this series, so it only applies to systems with at least five gas cylinders, such as transit buses or heavy trucks. The module notices that the coil draws no current when commanded. No manufacturer documents P2A2E publicly, and TransEco's AFCM table lists valve E only with its Low and High codes. New Flyer offers a practical check: if the engine fails to start, confirm that the door of the fill box is shut and the solenoid wires are plugged in, because an open door also keeps all tank valves shut. Swapping the coil with a neighbour tells a coil fault from a wiring fault. CARB's monitoring rules for output components apply.

Title: DTC P2324 - Ignition Coil I Primary Control Circuit Low
Diagnostic Codes: P2324
Vehicle System: Engine And Transmission
Problem Description: Coil I is the ninth coil, so P2324 only appears on ten- or twelve-cylinder petrol engines. The documented user is Ford: its OBD system summaries (2012 and 2020–2023) group P2324 with the other codes for a coil driver shorted to ground, monitored continuously from 200 rpm with the battery between 11 and 16 V, and Ford's 2014 code interpretation list marks it as a MIL code. The candidate engine in Ford's range is the 6.8-litre Modular V10 of the E-Series and heavy trucks, for which Ford also specifies a 40-1 crank wheel. After a driver fault the PCM shuts the injector of that cylinder for 30 s and retries. GM's tables end at coil H, so no GM engine uses this code. Opens on coil I are P0359, misfire on cylinder 9 is P0309.

top_5.document:
Title: DTC P0D17 - Battery Charging System A High Voltage Interlock Circuit Low
Diagnostic Codes: P0D17
Vehicle System: Engine And Transmission
Problem Description: P0D17 means the sensed voltage of the charging HVIL loop is too low. GM documents the check for the Chevrolet Volt (2011, 2014) and the Cadillac ELR: while the module sources 5 V into the loop, a sensed value under 30 % of the reference in two samples out of two at 12.5 ms sets the code as Type A, with the MIL on after one trip. A low reading suggests a path to ground or leakage somewhere in the loop wiring, or a fault in the measuring stage of the module. Because the test only runs with the source switched on, it typically shows up around charging. The interlock of battery and drive has its own code, P0A0C. P0D18 is the high counterpart, P0D15 the open loop. With an implausible loop the car refuses to charge.
Symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp after one trip (GM Type A); Charging refused
Possible Causes: Interlock wire chafed and touching ground (likelihood: high); Moisture or dirt in an interlock connector causing leakage (likelihood: medium); Fault in the interlock source or measuring circuit of the control module (likelihood: low)

Title: DTC P0D47 - Battery Charger 14 Volt Output Current Sensor Circuit
Diagnostic Codes: P0D47
Vehicle System: Engine And Transmission
Problem Description: P0D47 is the general circuit code for the current sensor in the charger's 14 V output, the measurement of how much current the charger's internal low-voltage stage delivers. top_5.document:
Title: DTC P0D23 - Battery Charger A Output Shorted
Diagnostic Codes: P0D23
Vehicle System: Engine And Transmission
Problem Description: P0D23 points to a short on the high-voltage output side of the on-board charger. GM runs this check while the charger contactor is only in its precharge state and the multi-purpose contactor is open, a moment when almost no current should flow on the charger bus. If more than 0.35 A is measured there in four of five samples at 100 ms, with system voltage above 9 V or 10.2 V, the code is set as One Trip Type A in the Chevrolet Volt from 2011 and the Cadillac ELR up to 2016. The test is skipped while output current sensor faults are active or while thermal conditioning runs. A current at that stage suggests an internal short in the charger output, a damaged high-voltage cable or a stuck contactor path. Charging is blocked. Current deviations during normal charging are P0D22.
Symptoms: Charging refused immediately after plugging in; MIL on at once
Possible Causes: Internal short in the charger's high-voltage output stage (likelihood: high); Damaged high-voltage cable between charger and battery (likelihood: medium); Charging contactor path conducting when it should not (likelihood: low)
Diagnostic Steps: Connect OBD-II diagnostic scanner and verify active code P0D23 (Battery Charger A Output Shorted). Perform visual and physical inspection of affected components: battery charger a, wiring harness, hybrid control module. Check electrical wiring harnesses and connectors for looseness, corrosion, or pin displacement. Measure reference voltage, ground continuity, and component resistance against manufacturer specifications. Repair guidance: Professional technician service recommended. Estimated labor time: 1-5 hours
Recommended Actions: Prioritize inspection of primary cause: Internal short in the charger's high-voltage output stage (likelihood: high). If issue persists, inspect secondary potential fault: Damaged high-voltage cable between charger and battery (likelihood: medium). Due to system criticality, have vehicle inspected by an ASE-certified technician.

Title: DTC P0D17 - Battery Charging System A High Voltage Interlock Circuit Low
Diagnostic Codes: P0D17
Vehicle System: Engine And Transmission
Problem Description: P0D17 means the sensed voltage of the charging HVIL loop is too low. GM documents the check for the Chevrolet Volt (2011, 2014) and the Cadillac ELR: while the module sources 5 V into the loop, a sensed value under 30 % of the reference in two samples out of two at 12.5 ms sets the code as Type A, with the MIL on after one trip. A low reading suggests a path to ground or leakage somewhere in the loop wiring, or a fault in the measuring stage of the module. Because the test only runs with the source switched on, it typically shows up around charging. The interlock of battery and drive has its own code, P0A0C. P0D18 is the high counterpart, P0D15 the open loop. With an implausible loop the car refuses to charge.

Title: DTC P0DBD - Hybrid/EV Battery Cell Balancing Circuit E Stuck On
Diagnostic Codes: P0DBD
Vehicle System: Engine And Transmission
Problem Description: With P0DBD the controller finds circuit E active when it should be idle. LG Chem's EP2730933A1 offers a way to see it: with the balancing circuit commanded off, the voltage across the diagnosis resistor should match the idle pattern; if it looks like the active pattern, current is still flowing. Group E then loses charge around the clock and drifts below the others, which in time can block charging or limit power because the lowest cell sets the lower limit. A shorted transistor is the classic cause. Ford's hybrid BECM sets P0DBD as well; the 2017 OBD summary describes a 100 ms start-up test with open contactors in which any cell of circuit E deviating more than 75 mV from the mean marks the circuit. The circuit fault is P0DBC, the inactive case P0DBE.
Symptoms: MIL with battery warning; Power reduced as group E cells drop; Charge loss after a few days parked
Possible Causes: Balancing transistor of circuit E shorted (likelihood: high); Drive line of the switch held active by the monitoring chip (likelihood: medium); Leakage on the module board after moisture (likelihood: low)
Diagnostic Steps: Connect OBD-II diagnostic scanner and verify active code P0DBD (Hybrid/EV Battery Cell Balancing Circuit E Stuck On). Perform visual and physical inspection of affected components: hv battery cell balancing circuit e, bms. Check electrical wiring harnesses and connectors for looseness, corrosion, or pin displacement. Measure reference voltage, ground continuity, and component resistance against manufacturer specifications. Repair guidance: Professional technician service recommended. Title: DTC P0D49 - Battery Charger 14 Volt Output Current Sensor Circuit Low
Diagnostic Codes: P0D49
Vehicle System: Engine And Transmission
Problem Description: P0D49 reports that the current sensor in the charger's 14 V output reads too low. top_10.document:
Title: DTC P0D5B - Battery Charger 14 Volt Output Power Performance
Diagnostic Codes: P0D5B
Vehicle System: Engine And Transmission
Problem Description: P0D5B checks whether the power leaving the charger's built-in 14 V output is physically possible. GM's charger module for the Volt and ELR multiplies the measured 14 V output voltage and current and compares the product with the AC input power times a factor of about 2 plus an offset: 2.5 W in the 2011 table, 125 W in the 2014 Volt/ELR and 2016 ELR tables. Exceeding that for 1.6 s within a 2 s window sets a Type A fault with MIL. The test only runs when the sensor codes P0D44, P0D45, P0D49 and P0D4A are clear, and the same low-voltage power also enters GM's total output check P1ECE. Because the 12 V side only takes part while charging, failures mostly show up as charging faults.
Symptoms: MIL on (GM); Charging interrupted; 12 V battery not supported while plugged in
Possible Causes: Voltage or current measurement of the 14 V stage reads too high (likelihood: high); AC input power measured too low (likelihood: medium); Low-voltage stage of the on-board charger faulty (likelihood: medium)
Diagnostic Steps: Connect OBD-II diagnostic scanner and verify active code P0D5B (Battery Charger 14 Volt Output Power Performance). Perform visual and physical inspection of affected components: battery charger 14v output, on board charger. Check electrical wiring harnesses and connectors for looseness, corrosion, or pin displacement. Measure reference voltage, ground continuity, and component resistance against manufacturer specifications. Repair guidance: Professional technician service recommended. Estimated labor time: 0.5-4 hours
Recommended Actions: Prioritize inspection of primary cause: Voltage or current measurement of the 14 V stage reads too high (likelihood: high). If issue persists, inspect secondary potential fault: AC input power measured too low (likelihood: medium). Due to system criticality, have vehicle inspected by an ASE-certified technician.

Title: DTC P0D54 - Battery Charger Hybrid/EV Battery Output Current Sensor Circuit High
Diagnostic Codes: P0D54
Vehicle System: Engine And Transmission
Problem Description: P0D54 marks a current reading at the charger's high-voltage output that exceeds the sensor's upper limit. The limit sits well above normal charging current, so the value counts as an electrical fault rather than real current. GM's 2011 Volt charger module triggers at 18 A or more, the 2014 Volt/ELR table at 17.7 A, each over 400 of 500 ms and rated Type A with MIL. Mitsubishi's 2022 Outlander PHEV logs it as a short to supply once the sensor voltage exceeds 4.658 V, corresponding to roughly 54 A, for 0.5 s; charging is stopped and the charger/DC-DC unit replaced. While P0D54 is stored, GM suspends its output power plausibility test P0D5C. The low-side fault is P0D53.
Symptoms: AC charging interrupted or refused; MIL on (GM); Charge level stays unchanged after plugging in
Possible Causes: Current sensor output shorted to supply voltage in the charger (likelihood: high); Charger current measuring stage failed (likelihood: high); Sensor output stuck at its upper end (likelihood: low)
Diagnostic Steps: Connect OBD-II diagnostic scanner and verify active code P0D54 (Battery Charger Hybrid/EV Battery Output Current Sensor Circuit High). Perform visual and physical inspection of affected components: battery charger hv output current sensor, on board charger. Check electrical wiring harnesses and connectors for looseness, corrosion, or pin displacement. Measure reference voltage, ground continuity, and component resistance against manufacturer specifications. Repair guidance: Professional technician service recommended. Estimated labor time: 0.5-4 hours
Recommended Actions: Prioritize inspection of primary cause: Current sensor output shorted to supply voltage in the charger (likelihood: high). If issue persists, inspect secondary potential fault: Charger current measuring stage failed (likelihood: high). Due to system criticality, have vehicle inspected by an ASE-certified technician.

Title: DTC C0081 - ABS Malfunction Indicator
Diagnostic Codes: C0081
Vehicle System: Brakes And Suspension
Problem Description: Covers the ABS malfunction indicator (warning lamp) itself as driven or monitored by the ABS/ESC module. The module commands the ABS lamp on for a fault and off when healthy, and monitors the output circuit; this code is set when the lamp circuit is open or shorted, the lamp does not respond, or the commanded and observed states disagree, for example a bulb-check failure or a bus message not reaching the cluster. It is about the indicator path rather than the ABS hydraulics, so braking and ABS themselves may still work while the driver loses the warning. The related rear-axle mismatch and wheel-speed codes describe the faults the lamp would normally announce. No code-specific public bulletin was confirmed; the entry follows the SAE J2012 generic definition and warning-lamp output monitoring.
Symptoms: ABS warning lamp stuck on or off; Failed lamp self-check; Driver loses ABS warning
Possible Causes: Open or shorted indicator circuit (likelihood: high); Lamp request not reaching the cluster (likelihood: medium); Failed indicator bulb or driver (likelihood: low)
Diagnostic Steps: Connect OBD-II diagnostic scanner and verify active code C0081 (ABS Malfunction Indicator). Perform visual and physical inspection of affected components: wheel speed sensor rl, wheel speed sensor rr, tyres. Check electrical wiring harnesses and connectors for looseness, corrosion, or pin displacement. Measure reference voltage, ground continuity, and component resistance against manufacturer specifications. Repair guidance: DIY feasible. Estimated labor time: 0.3-2 hours
Recommended Actions: Prioritize inspection of primary cause: Open or shorted indicator circuit (likelihood: high). If issue persists, inspect secondary potential fault: Lamp request not reaching the cluster (likelihood: medium). Title: DTC C0075 - Brake Pedal Position Performance
Diagnostic Codes: C0075
Vehicle System: Brakes And Suspension
Problem Description: A performance code for the brake pedal position input, set when the signal is present but behaves implausibly, for example it does not change as expected, lags, or disagrees with brake pressure and the switch. The stability and brake modules use pedal position to blend regenerative and friction braking and to arm or cancel driver-assist functions. Manufacturers map this code to the input their system uses: Subaru documents C0075 as a concern with the wheel-cylinder pressure-sensor signal in the EyeSight dynamics-control hydraulic module, while some European systems tie it to the brake-light switch feeding the ESP unit. A fault degrades regenerative blending and assist functions and sets the ABS/ESC warning lamp while base braking remains. The entry follows the SAE J2012 generic definition.
Symptoms: Degraded regenerative braking blend; Driver-assist functions limited; ABS/ESC warning lamp on
Possible Causes: Pedal/pressure sensor signal implausible (likelihood: high); Pedal or switch out of adjustment (likelihood: medium); Harness or connector fault (likelihood: low)
Diagnostic Steps: Connect OBD-II diagnostic scanner and verify active code C0075 (Brake Pedal Position Performance). Perform visual and physical inspection of affected components: brake pedal sensor. Check electrical wiring harnesses and connectors for looseness, corrosion, or pin displacement. Measure reference voltage, ground continuity, and component resistance against manufacturer specifications. Repair guidance: Professional technician service recommended. Estimated labor time: 0.5-3 hours
Recommended Actions: Prioritize inspection of primary cause: Pedal/pressure sensor signal implausible (likelihood: high). If issue persists, inspect secondary potential fault: Pedal or switch out of adjustment (likelihood: medium). Due to system criticality, have vehicle inspected by an ASE-certified technician.

Title: DTC C0075 - Brake Pedal Position Performance
Diagnostic Codes: C0075
Vehicle System: Brakes And Suspension
Problem Description: A performance code for the brake pedal position input, set when the signal is present but behaves implausibly, for example it does not change as expected, lags, or disagrees with brake pressure and the switch. The stability and brake modules use pedal position to blend regenerative and friction braking and to arm or cancel driver-assist functions. Manufacturers map this code to the input their system uses: Subaru documents C0075 as a concern with the wheel-cylinder pressure-sensor signal in the EyeSight dynamics-control hydraulic module, while some European systems tie it to the brake-light switch feeding the ESP unit. A fault degrades regenerative blending and assist functions and sets the ABS/ESC warning lamp while base braking remains. The entry follows the SAE J2012 generic definition.
Symptoms: Degraded regenerative braking blend; Driver-assist functions limited; ABS/ESC warning lamp on
Possible Causes: Pedal/pressure sensor signal implausible (likelihood: high); Pedal or switch out of adjustment (likelihood: medium); Harness or connector fault (likelihood: low)
Diagnostic Steps: Connect OBD-II diagnostic scanner and verify active code C0075 (Brake Pedal Position Performance). Perform visual and physical inspection of affected components: brake pedal sensor. Check electrical wiring harnesses and connectors for looseness, corrosion, or pin displacement. Measure reference voltage, ground continuity, and component resistance against manufacturer specifications. Repair guidance: Professional technician service recommended. Estimated labor time: 0.5-3 hours
Recommended Actions: Prioritize inspection of primary cause: Pedal/pressure sensor signal implausible (likelihood: high). If issue persists, inspect secondary potential fault: Pedal or switch out of adjustment (likelihood: medium). Due to system criticality, have vehicle inspected by an ASE-certified technician.

Title: DTC C0056 - Left Rear Wheel Speed Sensor Circuit Intermittent
Diagnostic Codes: C0056
Vehicle System: Brakes And Suspension
Problem Description: Covers an intermittent fault in the left rear wheel speed sensor circuit, where the signal is lost or corrupted only part of the time rather than permanently. The ABS/ESC module expects a clean pulse train proportional to wheel speed; a chafed wire that opens over bumps, a loose or corroded connector, a cracked sensor or a contaminated encoder ring can make the signal drop out briefly. Because the fault is sporadic it may set and self-clear, and ABS, traction and stability control drop out only during the glitches. The ABS warning lamp is set and base braking remains. Bosch active wheel speed sensors depend on a stable two-wire supply and a clean air gap to the encoder. No code-specific public bulletin was confirmed; the entry follows the SAE J2012 generic definition.
Symptoms: Intermittent ABS warning lamp; ABS/ESC drops out briefly; Speedometer flickers
Possible Causes: Chafed wire or loose connector (likelihood: high); Cracked sensor or contaminated encoder (likelihood: medium); Excessive or varying air gap (likelihood: low)
Diagnostic Steps: Connect OBD-II diagnostic scanner and verify active code C0056 (Left Rear Wheel Speed Sensor Circuit Intermittent). Perform visual and physical inspection of affected components: wheel speed sensor rl, sensor wiring. Check electrical wiring harnesses and connectors for looseness, corrosion, or pin displacement. Measure reference voltage, ground continuity, and component resistance against manufacturer specifications. Repair guidance: DIY feasible. Estimated labor time: 0.5-2.5 hours
Recommended Actions: Prioritize inspection of primary cause: Chafed wire or loose connector (likelihood: high). If issue persists, inspect secondary potential fault: Cracked sensor or contaminated encoder (likelihood: medium). Clear diagnostic trouble codes with scanner after component repair and perform a verification test drive.

Title: DTC P2711 - Unexpected Mechanical Gear Disengagement
Diagnostic Codes: P2711
Vehicle System: Engine And Transmission
Problem Description: P2711 is set when the transmission controller sees the drivetrain act as if a gear were no longer properly engaged although it never commanded that, for example because a clutch drags or a gear does not engage as selected. Volkswagen Group uses it on DSG gearboxes: Audi bulletin 2029069 for the 2009-2010 A3 and TT logs it as 19143 P2711 004, with a lit gear display and shudder on the first launch, and blames a clutch that drags too strongly; VW bulletin 2028714 for 2009-2012 Jetta, Golf, CC, Eos and 2012 Passat with the 02E calls it an implausible shift sequence, caused by debris in the clutch pack, where the selected gear may not engage after start-up. Both replace the multiple clutch (beyond about 18,500 or 19,000 miles); improved clutches entered production in March 2010.
Symptoms: Gear indicator flashing or lit in the cluster; Shudder on the first drive-away; Selected Drive or Reverse does not engage after start-up
Possible Causes: Excessive drag torque in the dual clutch (worn or early-production plates) (likelihood: high); Debris inside the clutch assembly (likelihood: medium); Shift fork or gear actuator not holding the gear (likelihood: low)
Diagnostic Steps: Connect OBD-II diagnostic scanner and verify active code P2711 (Unexpected Mechanical Gear Disengagement). Perform visual and physical inspection of affected components: transmission internal, hydraulic control unit. Check electrical wiring harnesses and connectors for looseness, corrosion, or pin displacement. Measure reference voltage, ground continuity, and component resistance against manufacturer specifications. Repair guidance: Professional technician service recommended. Estimated labor time: 4-12 hours
Recommended Actions: Prioritize inspection of primary cause: Excessive drag torque in the dual clutch (worn or early-production plates) (likelihood: high). If issue persists, inspect secondary potential fault: Debris inside the clutch assembly (likelihood: medium). Due to system criticality, have vehicle inspected by an ASE-certified technician.

Title: DTC P0733 - Gear 3 Incorrect Ratio
Diagnostic Codes: P0733
Vehicle System: Engine And Transmission
Problem Description: The transmission module divides input (turbine) speed by output speed and compares the result with the ratio of the commanded gear; a deviation means slip – a clutch or brake not holding, too little pressure – or a wrong gear. Thresholds: Ford more than 30 rpm off for 1.8 s three times (diesel 2023: over 20 % for 12 s), GM's 2006 tables and the Allison 1000 converter slip of 200–230 rpm for 2.25 s after one trip, Saab's Aisin boxes over 20 % twelve times without MIL. P0733 concerns third gear. Slip typically shows as flare on the 2–3 shift. If fourth or fifth gear shows the ratio of third, Aisin-type logic sets P0730 instead. Ford stores it only if the fault fits no particular solenoid. On GM manual transmissions it checks the gear position sensor.
Symptoms: Slipping or flare in third gear, engine speed higher than expected; Harsh or delayed shifts; Limp mode (Aisin: second gear and reverse only), transmission warning; Check engine light depending on manufacturer
Possible Causes: Fluid level too low or fluid worn or contaminated (likelihood: high); Clutch or brake for third gear worn (linings, piston seal) (likelihood: high); Sticking shift or pressure valve, leaking valve body gasket, blocked passages (likelihood: medium); GM manual transmissions only: gear position sensor faulty or not learned (likelihood: medium)
Diagnostic Steps: Connect OBD-II diagnostic scanner and verify active code P0733 (Gear 3 Incorrect Ratio). Perform visual and physical inspection of affected components: transmission clutches, transmission valve body, transmission fluid, transmission control module. Check electrical wiring harnesses and connectors for looseness, corrosion, or pin displacement. Measure reference voltage, ground continuity, and component resistance against manufacturer specifications. Repair guidance: Professional technician service recommended. Estimated labor time: 0.5-14 hours
Recommended Actions: Prioritize inspection of primary cause: Fluid level too low or fluid worn or contaminated (likelihood: high). If issue persists, inspect secondary potential fault: Clutch or brake for third gear worn (linings, piston seal) (likelihood: high). Due to system criticality, have vehicle inspected by an ASE-certified technician.

Title: DTC P2E14 - Gear Selection Actuator Position Sensor Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
Diagnostic Codes: P2E14
Vehicle System: Engine And Transmission
Problem Description: P2E14 covers a position signal from the gear selection actuator that is present but unsteady: it drops out for moments, jumps or carries an implausible frequency or pattern, without staying low or high long enough for P2E12 or P2E13. No manufacturer documents P2E14 publicly. Two related checks show what erratic means in practice. GM's 2023 dual-clutch TCM tables reject a rod position sensor whose carrier frequency leaves the 1500 to 2500 Hz band for 150 ms (P2835, Type A). Ford's 2012 DPS6 summary watches the three Hall signals of each shift drum motor and sets P2835 if their sequence comes out of order. Loose pins, harness chafing that only touches under vibration, and electrical noise are typical. Drivers notice sporadic refused shifts or brief neutral drops that later vanish.
Symptoms: Occasional refused or delayed shifts; Short drops to neutral while driving; Warning lamp that comes and goes
Possible Causes: Loose or fretted terminal in the actuator connector (likelihood: high); Harness chafing that only shorts or opens under vibration or heat (likelihood: medium); Interference from damaged shielding or nearby motor wiring (likelihood: low); Sensor with an internal intermittent fault (likelihood: low)
Diagnostic Steps: Connect OBD-II diagnostic scanner and verify active code P2E14 (Gear Selection Actuator Position Sensor Circuit Intermittent/Erratic). Perform visual and physical inspection of affected components: gear selection actuator position sensor, wiring harness, tcm. Check electrical wiring harnesses and connectors for looseness, corrosion, or pin displacement. Measure reference voltage, ground continuity, and component resistance against manufacturer specifications. Repair guidance: Professional technician service recommended. Estimated labor time: 1-5 hours
Recommended Actions: Prioritize inspection of primary cause: Loose or fretted terminal in the actuator connector (likelihood: high). If issue persists, inspect secondary potential fault: Harness chafing that only shorts or opens under vibration or heat (likelihood: medium). Due to system criticality, have vehicle inspected by an ASE-certified technician.
